source.title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows

accepted.question_text: For the Directed Feedback Vertex Set problem on planar directed graphs, where the input is a directed graph G and a positive integer k and the task is to decide whether there exists a set S of k vertices such that every directed cycle of G contains a member of S, does there exist a fixed-parameter algorithm whose dependence on k is single exponential?
accepted.context_brief: Directed Feedback Vertex Set on planar digraphs

evidence.quote: Question: Is there a set S of k vertices such that each directed cycle of G contains a member of S?
It remains open if there exist a single exponential algorithm for Directed Feedback Vertex Set even on planar graphs.

accepted.question_text: For the Directed Feedback Vertex Set problem, where the input is a directed graph G and a positive integer k and the task is to decide whether there exists a set S of k vertices such that every directed cycle of G contains a member of S, does the problem admit a polynomial kernel when parameterized by k?

evidence.quote: Question: Is there a set S of k vertices such that each directed cycle of G contains a member of S?
The existence of polynomial kernel is also open.

accepted.question_text: Given a directed planar graph G together with k ordered pairs of vertices (r1, s1), ..., (rk, sk), is there a fixed-parameter algorithm in k that decides whether G contains k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths P1, ..., Pk such that Pi runs from ri to si for every i?

evidence.quote: Question: Does G have k vertex-disjoint paths P1,...,Pk with Pi running from ri to si?

accepted.question_text: Given an n-bit prime p, a generator g of the multiplicative group F*_p, an element a in F*_p, and a positive integer k, is there a positive integer x whose binary representation contains at most k ones such that a = g^x?

evidence.quote: Question: Is there a positive integer x whose binary representation has at most k 1's (that is, x has a Hamming weight of k) such that a = gx?
Bounded Hamming Weight Discrete Logarithm Open

accepted.question_text: Given a k-polymatroid M, is there a fixed-parameter algorithm in k that decides whether M is hypergraphic, meaning that M is the hypergraphic polymatroid of some hypergraph?

Given a finite poset Q and a finite poset P, is there a fixed-parameter algorithm parameterized by P that decides whether P is a chain minor of Q, that is, whether there exists a partial mapping from the ground set of Q to the ground set of P such that every chain of P is the image of some chain of Q under that mapping?

evidence.quote: Question: Is P a chain minor of Q?

accepted.question_text: Given an undirected graph G with two distinguished vertices v1 and v2 and a positive integer k, does player one have a winning strategy in Generalized Hex that wins within at most k moves, where players alternately place white and black pebbles on unoccupied vertices and player one wins by creating a white path from v1 to v2?

evidence.quote: Question: Does player one have a winning strategy of at most k moves in Generalized Hex?
To the best of our knowledge, the problem remains open.

accepted.question_text: Given two collections of k multivariate polynomials p1, ..., pk and q1, ..., qk, each represented by listing the monomials with nonzero coefficients, is there a deterministic fixed-parameter algorithm in k for deciding whether the polynomial identity product_{i=1}^k p_i = product_{i=1}^k q_i holds?

evidence.quote: Question: Does the following identity hold?
It could still be a nontrivial question if the problem is in deterministic FPT.

accepted.question_text: Given an undirected red/blue bipartite graph G = (R, B, E) and a positive integer k, is there a nonempty subset R' of R of size at most k such that every vertex in B has an even number of neighbors in R'?

evidence.quote: Question: Is there a non-empty set of at most k vertices R ⊆ R, such that each member of B has an even number of neighbors in R?

needs_review.question_text_raw: It could be interesting to investigate the problem for other ℓ_p norms as well.

evidence.quote: It could be interesting to investigate the problem for other ℓp norms as well.

trace.notes: Mapped the PDF into Introduction, A Lineup of FPT Suspects, A Lineup of Tough Customers, Acknowledgement, and References; open items were concentrated on pages 459 and 461-466.
Scanned the FPT Suspects section and extracted the two explicit follow-up open questions for Directed Feedback Vertex Set plus the explicitly open Planar Directed Disjoint Paths item.

Scanned the Tough Customers section and extracted the explicitly open items Bounded Hamming Weight Discrete Logarithm, Polymatroid Recognition, Chain Minor Ordering, Short Generalized Hex, Polynomial Product Identity, Shortest Vector follow-up, and Even Set.
Expanded the planar Directed Feedback Vertex Set follow-up into a self-contained algorithmic question using the boxed problem statement plus the open-status sentence.
Expanded the kernelization follow-up for Directed Feedback Vertex Set into a self-contained parameterized question.
Rewrote the Planar Directed Disjoint Paths box into a standalone FPT question with its terminal-pair notation inlined.
Kept the bounded-Hamming-weight discrete logarithm statement close to the source because the source already states the full problem self-containedly.
Inlined the meaning of hypergraphic from the surrounding paragraph to keep the recognition problem self-contained.
Expanded the chain minor question with the source's partial-mapping characterization.
Inlined the Generalized Hex move rules and win condition from the source paragraph.
Specialized the open issue for Polynomial Product Identity to the deterministic-FPT question stated in the discussion paragraph.
Renamed the quantified subset to R' in the rewrite to avoid collision with the source's bipartition symbol R while preserving the same mathematical condition.

The Shortest Vector follow-up about other ℓ_p norms was extracted but not accepted because the source does not formulate a precise parameterized question or specify the target norm family sufficiently for a faithful standalone rewrite.
No near-duplicate accepted questions were found; the two Directed Feedback Vertex Set follow-ups were kept separate because one concerns running time and the other kernelization.
Accepted items have explicit page-cited quotes and self-contained rewrites grounded in the chapter text. The vague Shortest Vector follow-up failed the precision gate and was moved to needs_review.
